blocks.text: 试点概况

inlines.text: 试点概况

blocks.text: 这是一次为期六周的初步试点。其间，我们团队成员将在 OpenAI 现场办公，对其训练后对齐评估开展独立评估。我们将审查这些评估的范围与质量，并向公司和公众提供独立见解。

inlines.text: 这是一次为期六周的初步试点。其间，我们团队成员将在 OpenAI 现场办公，对其训练后对齐评估开展独立评估。我们将审查这些评估的范围与质量，并向公司和公众提供独立见解。

blocks.text: 我们已谈妥对若干 OpenAI 模型的特权访问，包括查看原始思维链。我们团队还将审查 OpenAI 用于评估模型对齐、发现模型欺骗、操纵和奖励黑客等问题的部分非公开内部评估。

blocks.text: 嵌入 OpenAI 环境能让我们接触到外部评估者通常无法获取的内部信息。但这并不等同于“员工级”或“类员工”访问权限。

blocks.text: 这次试点只是第一步。我们已与 OpenAI 商定，计划在 2027 年初开展更完整的 OpenAI 对齐评估，届时将依托更广泛、更深入的嵌入式访问。具体细节尚未敲定，但我们期待从这次试点中汲取经验。

blocks.text: 试点条款

inlines.text: 试点条款

blocks.text: 我们认为，公开我们所处的条件、说明这些条件可能如何影响独立评估，十分重要。

inlines.text: 我们认为，公开我们所处的条件、说明这些条件可能如何影响独立评估，十分重要。

blocks.text: 本协议的条款包括：

inlines.text: 本协议的条款包括：
访问权限

。从 12 月初开始，我们的员工将在六周内获得对若干 OpenAI 模型的特权访问，其中至少包括一个仅限内部使用的模型，并可查看原始思维链输出。我们的员工还将获准审查部分训练后对齐评估、大量以往训练和评估运行的记录，以及安全案例文档。我们可以随时申请更多权限，由 OpenAI 决定是否批准。我们将公开说明我们申请了什么、哪些获批或遭拒，以及这对我们的结论有何影响。我们还可以对可用模型使用部分自有工具和评估。
报酬
。Transluce 及其员工不就本次试点向 OpenAI 收取费用。OpenAI 将承担算力成本，提供现场设备和基础设施，并为我们的驻场员工提供临时办公空间。
人员筛选
。OpenAI 必须在试点前审核并批准 Transluce 的驻场人员。OpenAI 可就安全、保密和利益冲突相关问题进行筛查。
升级机制
。关于访问权限、内容删减或其他条件的分歧，首先提交给我们的 OpenAI 对接人，之后可升级至 OpenAI 高管以及安全与安保委员会——这是 OpenAI 基金会董事会下属的独立监督委员会。若仍无法解决，我们也可直接向该委员会提出关切。

inlines.text: 发布细节

blocks.text: 我们无法准确预判最终报告会包含哪些内容，但我们的意图是尽可能透明地公开我们的方法和发现。

blocks.text: Transluce 对我们的报告拥有编辑控制权，但有两项重要限制：

inlines.text: Transluce 对我们的报告拥有编辑控制权，但有两项重要限制：
非公开信息的删减
。协议赋予 OpenAI 在报告发布前提前收到报告的权利，并可要求删减知识产权及其他非公开信息。这可能会限制我们分享支撑结论的完整证据，不过如果 OpenAI 的限制对我们的结论造成了实质性影响，我们可以公开说明。
与仅限内部使用的模型相关的限制
。协议禁止我们发布与仅限内部使用的模型相关的结果，因此我们公开提供的所有信息都将涉及对已发布模型所做的评估。

blocks.text: 我们调查结果的完整、未经删减版本将提交给 OpenAI 基金会董事会的安全与安保委员会。

blocks.text: 关于 Transluce

inlines.text: 关于 Transluce

blocks.text: Transluce 是一家非营利研究实验室，致力于引导 AI 的发展服务于公共利益。我们开展研究与评估，以增进公众对 AI 模型行为的理解，涵盖失控智能体、儿童安全和操纵等领域。我们还构建开放、易用的工具来支持这类研究，推动形成成熟的独立 AI 监督与问责生态。

blocks.text: Pilot overview

inlines.text: Pilot overview

blocks.text: This initial exercise is a six-week pilot where members of our team will work onsite at OpenAI to conduct an independent assessment of its internal post-training alignment evaluations. We will review the scope and quality of those evaluations and provide independent insights to the company and to the public.

blocks.text: We have negotiated privileged access to a handful of OpenAI models, including access to raw chains of thought. Our team will also review select, non-public internal evaluations that OpenAI uses to assess model alignment and detect issues like model deception, manipulation, and reward hacking.

blocks.text: The terms of the pilot

inlines.text: The terms of the pilot

blocks.text: We believe that it is important to be transparent about the conditions we’re operating under and clarify how they might impact our independent assessment.

inlines.text: We believe that it is important to be transparent about the conditions we’re operating under and clarify how they might impact our independent assessment.

blocks.text: The terms of this agreement include the following:

inlines.text: The terms of this agreement include the following:
Access

. Starting in early December, our staff will have six weeks of privileged access to a handful of OpenAI models, including at least one internal-only model and the ability to review raw chain-of-thought outputs. Our staff will also have permission to review select post-training alignment evaluations, a large number of transcripts from previous training and evaluation runs, and safety case documentation. We can request more access as we go, and OpenAI decides whether we get it. We will report publicly what we requested, what was approved or declined, and how this affected our conclusions. We also have the ability to use some of our own tooling and evaluations on the available models.
Compensation

. Transluce and its staff are not accepting payment from OpenAI for this pilot. OpenAI will cover the cost of compute, provide on-site devices and infrastructure, and make available temporary workspace for our embedded staff.
Staff selection
. OpenAI must review and approve the embedded Transluce staff members prior to the pilot. OpenAI can screen for issues related to security, confidentiality, and conflicts of interest.
Escalation

. Disagreements about access, redactions, or other conditions go first to our OpenAI point of contact and can then be escalated to OpenAI executives and the Safety and Security Committee, an independent oversight committee of the OpenAI Foundation's Board. If that is insufficient, we can also raise concerns with the Committee directly.

blocks.text: Publication details

inlines.text: Publication details

blocks.text: We cannot predict exactly what will be included in our final report, but our intention is to provide as much transparency as possible about our methods and findings.

inlines.text: We cannot predict exactly what will be included in our final report, but our intention is to provide as much transparency as possible about our methods and findings.

blocks.text: Transluce has editorial control over our report, but there are two important restrictions:

inlines.text: Transluce has editorial control over our report, but there are two important restrictions:
Redaction of non-public information

. The agreement gives OpenAI the right to receive our report in advance of release and to request redactions of intellectual property and other non-public information. This could constrain our ability to share full evidence for our claims, though we can publicly share if OpenAI’s restrictions meaningfully impacted our conclusions.
Restriction related to internal-only models
. The agreement prevents us from publishing results related to internal-only models, so all the information we provide publicly will be related to assessments conducted on released models.

blocks.text: The complete, unredacted version of our findings will be provided to the OpenAI Foundation Board’s Safety and Security Committee.

blocks.text: To provide additional transparency, in the final report we will document the conditions we operated under, relying on the AEF-1 standard published by the AI Evaluator Forum. For more details on how we preserve our independence as evaluators, see also our Independence and Transparency Policy.

blocks.text: About Transluce

inlines.text: About Transluce

blocks.text: Transluce is a nonprofit research lab dedicated to steering AI’s development in the public interest. We conduct research and evaluations to improve public understanding of AI model behaviors, including in areas like rogue agents, child safety, and manipulation. We also build open and accessible tools to facilitate this research and advance a mature ecosystem of independent AI oversight and accountability.
